metadata.title: Implement Fixes
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Apply the approved fixes from the fix plan to the codebase, commit changes with a conventional commit message referencing the PR, and push to the remote branch. Only implements 'Valid' category fixes from the approved plan.

output.description: Code changes committed and pushed to remote branch

prerequisites: Approved fix plan available in memory from analyze-plan-fixes step
Local workspace on the correct PR branch
Git remote configured and push access available
specificActions: Follow the substeps below in sequence
Workflow: read approved plan → apply code fixes → stage files → commit → push → store results
Only implement fixes categorized as 'Valid' in the approved plan
For 'Partial' fixes: implement only what was explicitly approved, note what was deferred
For 'Disagree' items: do NOT modify code — these are handled by reply-to-comments
Use Edit tool for precise code changes — do not overwrite entire files
Stage specific files with git add, not git add -A

read: Source code files to be modified
update: Source code files identified in the fix plan

tools: Edit - Apply precise code changes to affected files
Read - Read current file state before editing
bestPractices: Read the current file state before applying each fix to ensure the code hasn't drifted
Apply fixes one file at a time, verifying each change
Stage specific modified files by name — never use git add -A or git add .
Use conventional commit format with PR reference: fix: address PR #{prId} review comments
Include bullet points in commit message body describing each fix
Do not force push — if push fails, report the error
If a fix cannot be applied cleanly (code has changed), log the issue and skip that fix

substeps.name: Read Approved Fix Plan
substeps.description: Load the approved fixes from memory
actions: Read fixPlan.comments from memory
Filter to only 'Valid' and approved 'Partial' comments
Build a list of fixes to apply, each with: filePath, lineRange, proposedFix
Log: 'Implementing {count} fixes across {fileCount} files'

substeps.name: Apply Code Changes
substeps.description: Edit each affected file with the proposed fix
actions: For each fix to apply:
- Read the current file to verify the code context still matches
- Apply the proposed fix using Edit tool
- If the code has drifted and the fix can't apply cleanly: log warning and skip
- Log: 'Applied fix for comment #{threadId} in {filePath}'
Track list of files successfully modified and any skipped fixes

substeps.name: Stage and Commit
substeps.description: Stage modified files and create a conventional commit
actions: Stage each modified file individually with git add {filePath}
Create commit with message format:
Subject: fix: address PR #{prId} review comments
Body: bullet list of changes (one per fix)
If no files were modified (all fixes skipped): log warning and skip commit
Log: 'Committed {count} file changes'

substeps.name: Push to Remote
substeps.description: Push the commit to the remote branch
actions: Run git push to push the commit
If push fails: report the error — do NOT force push
If push succeeds: extract the commit hash
Log: 'Pushed commit {hash} to remote'

substeps.name: Store Results in Memory
substeps.description: Record implementation details for downstream steps
actions: Write to memory: implementation.filesModified (list of modified file paths), implementation.commitHash, implementation.commitMessage
Note any fixes that were skipped and why

substeps.name: End-Step: Compliance Check
substeps.description: Verify principles were followed in this step
actions: Verify: Was log.json updated for any user interactions?
Verify: Were mandatory actions confirmed with output?
Verify: All Valid fixes were applied or skipped with documented reason
Output: 'Step completed in compliance with operating principles'

flow.description: Linear flow: Read approved plan → Apply code changes per fix → Stage specific files → Commit with conventional message → Push to remote → Store results → Compliance check. If code has drifted, skip individual fixes with warning.

fields: Decisions Made: Which fixes to skip (if code drifted)
Notes: Skipped fixes with reasons, push success/failure

requiredFiles: Source code files referenced in fix plan
